narrativeReportMd:
# Count R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Count` has one local hard validation break: R6 strengthens the local `cnt-3` invariant so a primitive `Count.value` must be non-negative. An R4 instance fragment such as `{ "value": -1, "system": "http://unitsofmeasure.org", "code": "1" }` can satisfy the R4 `Count` invariant but fails the R6 expression.

## Scope
The R4 and R6 `StructureDefinition/Count` files were compared directly. Both artifacts exist and retain the same identity: canonical URL, type name, kind, derivation, base definition, and abstract flag. Changes inherited from `Quantity` and more general base artifacts are excluded from `findings[]` under the assignment scope rule.

## Main migration themes
The local migration issue is data cleansing rather than structural remapping: systems must identify negative count values and decide whether to reject, correct, or map them with an extension/profile-specific policy. The R6 definition also no longer carries the old XPath representation for the local invariant, so validators should use the FHIRPath expression.

## Highest-impact findings
The only hard instance-breaking local finding is `Count:VALUE_CONSTRAINT:Count.cnt-3:nonnegative`. It affects R4-to-R6 validation for negative integer counts. It should be rare in semantically clean data, but it is a real validator-visible change.

## Findings requiring human review
No local finding requires mandatory human review, although negative counts in migrated production data may need business or clinical policy review because an automated transform cannot infer the intended correction.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The non-negative requirement is probably justified for a datatype named `Count`. A less disruptive rollout could have used a warning invariant or profile before changing the base datatype rule, but that would leave the base R6 datatype less semantically precise.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze `Quantity` for inherited comparator and UCUM-warning changes, and analyze `Element`/`DataType`/`Extension` for inherited base-model and extension-governance changes.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Count` keeps the same identity and element shape, but R6 locally tightens `cnt-3` to reject negative primitive values. The main migration concern is finding and remediating negative count data; inherited `Quantity` comparator changes are out of scope for this report. Confidence is high for the computable StructureDefinition delta, with rationale confidence limited by absent official change notes.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is mostly validation-policy work. Existing non-negative whole-number counts should continue to validate. Negative whole-number counts that slipped through R4 validation must be rejected, corrected, or carried through an explicit local policy. Validator/tooling migration should also move from any R4 XPath handling of `cnt-3` to the R6 FHIRPath constraint.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high because the R4 and R6 `Count` StructureDefinitions are present locally and the local differential contains only the root `Count` element. The non-negative requirement is directly visible in the R6 `cnt-3` FHIRPath expression. Confidence in the standards rationale is lower because no official diff or ballot explanation was included in the local inputs.

findings.title: R6 Count requires primitive values to be non-negative

oldState.summary: R4 `cnt-3` required a code when a value is present, UCUM system if system is present, code `1` if code is present, and a whole-number value; it did not explicitly reject negative whole numbers.

constraints.expression: (code.exists() or value.empty()) and (system.empty() or system = %ucum) and (code.empty() or code = '1') and (value.empty() or value.hasValue().not() or value.toString().contains('.').not())
constraints.human: There SHALL be a code with a value of "1" if there is a value. If system is present, it SHALL be UCUM.  If present, the value SHALL be a whole number.

semanticText.definition: A measured amount (or an amount that can potentially be measured). Note that measured amounts include amounts that are not precisely quantified, including amounts involving arbitrary units and floating currencies.
semanticText.comment: The context of use may frequently define what kind of quantity this is and therefore what kind of units can be used. The context of use may also restrict the values for the comparator.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 constrained `Count` values to be whole numbers when a primitive numeric value exists, with UCUM/code rules, but a value like `-1` was not excluded by the local `cnt-3` FHIRPath expression.

newState.summary: R6 `cnt-3` keeps the R4 rules and adds a primitive numeric value test requiring `value >= 0`.

constraints.expression: (code.exists() or value.empty()) and (system.empty() or system = %ucum) and (code.empty() or code = '1') and (value.empty() or value.hasValue().not() or value.toString().contains('.').not()) and (value.empty() or value.hasValue().not() or value >= 0)
constraints.human: There SHALL be a code with a value of "1" if there is a value. If system is present, it SHALL be UCUM.  If present, the value SHALL be a whole number.

semanticText.definition: A measured amount (or an amount that can potentially be measured). Note that measured amounts include amounts that are not precisely quantified, including amounts involving arbitrary units and floating currencies.
semanticText.comment: The context of use may frequently define what kind of quantity this is and therefore what kind of units can be used. The context of use may also restrict the values for the comparator.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes non-negativity part of the base `Count` validation rule. The human-readable constraint text was not updated to mention the non-negative requirement, but the computable FHIRPath expression is stricter.

facts.oldValue: (code.exists() or value.empty()) and (system.empty() or system = %ucum) and (code.empty() or code = '1') and (value.empty() or value.hasValue().not() or value.toString().contains('.').not())
facts.newValue: (code.exists() or value.empty()) and (system.empty() or system = %ucum) and (code.empty() or code = '1') and (value.empty() or value.hasValue().not() or value.toString().contains('.').not()) and (value.empty() or value.hasValue().not() or value >= 0)
facts.note: R6 appends a non-negative value check to the local `Count` invariant.

facts.oldValue: whole number, including negative whole numbers by expression
facts.note: The check applies when `value` exists and has a primitive value.
The breaking rule is visible in the computable expression rather than the human text.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The invariant key `cnt-3` is present on the root `Count` element in both R4 and R6 with the same core human text and an expression that is identical except for the appended `value >= 0` clause.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validator-visible tightening. An R4 `Count` with `value: -1`, `system: "http://unitsofmeasure.org"`, and `code: "1"` can pass the R4 `cnt-3` expression because it has a code, the system is UCUM, the code is `1`, and the string form does not contain a decimal point. The same fragment fails R6 because `value >= 0` is false. R6-valid non-negative counts remain representable in R4, so the local round-trip risk is low.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Negative counts are likely erroneous or semantically unusual, but rejecting historical data can still affect migration workflows, data quality dashboards, or integrations that previously stored sentinel negative values.

justification.inferredGoal: Make the computable `Count` datatype match the ordinary semantic expectation that a count cannot be negative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4-compatible base error invariant and add a base best-practice warning for negative counts, with stricter profiles where needed.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: a `Count` is ordinarily a cardinal quantity and negative primitive counts are semantically suspect. The R6 invariant creates a real R4-to-R6 validation break, but it affects the narrow case of negative whole-number counts that were R4-valid mainly because the old expression omitted the non-negative check. A warning/profile transition path would reduce migration disruption, but it would not make all base R6 `Count` instances enforce the core semantic rule, so the break is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would leave the R4 `cnt-3` error invariant intact and add a separate best-practice warning for `value < 0`; implementation guides or profiles could then make non-negativity mandatory where needed. That would preserve all R4-valid `Count` fragments, including negative sentinel or erroneous legacy values, and give implementers a migration runway. The alternative is only partial because base R6 would still allow negative counts and enforcement would fragment across profiles and local validation policies.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves negative historical values but leaves base R6 Count semantically permissive and shifts hard enforcement to profiles or local policy.

evidence.detail: R4 `cnt-3` lacks a non-negative numeric value test.
evidence.quote: (code.exists() or value.empty()) and (system.empty() or system = %ucum) and (code.empty() or code = '1') and (value.empty() or value.hasValue().not() or value.toString().contains('.').not())

evidence.detail: R6 `cnt-3` adds `value >= 0` when a primitive value is present.
The changed invariant is sourced to `StructureDefinition/Count`, not merely inherited from `Quantity`.

examples.examplesMd: The example is a datatype fragment, not a complete resource. It illustrates the local `Count` fields relevant to `cnt-3`: R4 permits the negative whole-number value by the invariant expression, while R6 rejects it. The migration example shows a syntactically valid non-negative replacement only; real correction requires domain-specific review.

findings.narrativeMd: `Count` now has an explicit computable non-negative requirement. This matters for migrations because a negative value that was accepted by strict R4 validation can become invalid without any element rename or cardinality change. The change is easy to miss because the element list is unchanged and the human-readable invariant text still says only that the value must be a whole number.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid data can become R6-invalid when `Count.value` is a primitive negative whole number. This is a hard instance-breaking R4-to-R6 validation change. It does not create a local R6-to-R4 representability problem because every R6 value satisfying the stricter non-negative constraint also fits the older R4 value domain. Strict validators, generated schema tests, and FHIRPath-based data quality checks should add negative-count fixtures.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan all migrated `Count` occurrences for negative primitive values before R6 validation. If negative values exist, do not blindly clamp them to zero unless the business meaning is clear. Prefer a data-quality remediation workflow: identify source system, determine whether the value was an error or sentinel, correct where authoritative, or preserve the exceptional meaning with a profile/extension outside base `Count` semantics. Add regression tests for `-1`, `0`, positive integers, decimal values, missing `code`, non-UCUM systems, and extension-only primitive values.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The base datatype could have remained backward compatible by using a warning invariant or requiring non-negativity only in profiles that need it. That alternative would avoid invalidating old records but would leave base R6 `Count` unable to enforce a fundamental semantic expectation. Given the datatype name and likely intent, the stricter rule is probably justified despite the migration break.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 human text for `cnt-3` still says only that the value must be a whole number. Reviewers may want to confirm whether the rendered specification text elsewhere documents the non-negative requirement.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 tightens the local `cnt-3` invariant so a `Count` with a primitive negative value, otherwise satisfying the R4 code/system/whole-number requirements, is no longer valid. That is an old-valid/new-invalid validation break, but it affects the narrow case of negative counts, which are semantically suspect for a type named `Count`. A concrete migration case is historical data or a local integration that used `Count.value = -1` as a sentinel or delta; it would need remapping before R6 validation. The tightening appears proportionate because accepting negative counts would weaken the computable meaning of the datatype, although the unchanged human text would be clearer if it explicitly mentioned non-negative values.
keyEvidence: R4 `StructureDefinition-Count.json` `snapshot.element[id=Count].constraint[key=cnt-3].expression` checks code/system and whole-number string form but has no `value >= 0` test.

R6 `StructureDefinition-Count.json` `snapshot.element[id=Count].constraint[key=cnt-3].expression` appends `(value.empty() or value.hasValue().not() or value >= 0)` with source `StructureDefinition/Count`.
R4 `StructureDefinition-Count.json` marks Count standards status as `trial-use`; local maturity data for Count also reports `standardsStatus: trial-use` and no numeric FMM.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The R4 baseline is trial-use rather than normative/FMM 5, and no numeric FMM was available locally. That softens the stability concern for a narrow semantic tightening; R6 becoming normative does not by itself increase the compatibility burden for R4 consumers.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4-valid negative whole-number Count instance can fail R6 validation because the R6 invariant now requires `value >= 0` when a primitive value is present.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could keep negative values valid and make non-negativity a warning or profile requirement, preserving sentinel/delta uses. That would undercut the core R6 goal of making Count computably non-negative in the base datatype, so the alternative has a real semantic and validation tradeoff rather than being an obviously better design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing hard-instance-breaking and no-less-breaking-alternative direction; the prior medium impact seems reasonable, with the added caveat that the unchanged invariant human text should ideally mention non-negativity.

findings.title: R6 Count no longer carries an XPath form for the local cnt-3 invariant

oldState.summary: R4 `cnt-3` included both a FHIRPath expression and an XPath expression in the local Count constraint metadata.

constraints.expression: (code.exists() or value.empty()) and (system.empty() or system = %ucum) and (code.empty() or code = '1') and (value.empty() or value.hasValue().not() or value.toString().contains('.').not())
constraints.human: There SHALL be a code with a value of "1" if there is a value. If system is present, it SHALL be UCUM.  If present, the value SHALL be a whole number.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 tooling could read an XPath representation from the `Count` StructureDefinition for XML-oriented constraint validation, in addition to the FHIRPath expression.

newState.summary: R6 `cnt-3` includes the FHIRPath expression and source but no XPath expression.

constraints.expression: (code.exists() or value.empty()) and (system.empty() or system = %ucum) and (code.empty() or code = '1') and (value.empty() or value.hasValue().not() or value.toString().contains('.').not()) and (value.empty() or value.hasValue().not() or value >= 0)
constraints.human: There SHALL be a code with a value of "1" if there is a value. If system is present, it SHALL be UCUM.  If present, the value SHALL be a whole number.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 validators and code generators must rely on the FHIRPath expression for this local invariant; the old XPath alternative is absent from the supplied R6 StructureDefinition.

facts.oldValue: (f:code or not(f:value)) and (not(exists(f:system)) or (f:system/@value='http://unitsofmeasure.org' and f:code/@value='1')) and not(contains(f:value/@value, '.'))
facts.note: The R6 local constraint omits the XPath representation present in R4.
FHIRPath remains available and is the authoritative computable expression in these inputs.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same invariant key `cnt-3` on the same root `Count` element is compared. The change is in the StructureDefinition metadata representation, not in the instance element tree.

impact.impactRationaleMd: No Count instance becomes valid or invalid solely because the XPath metadata is absent. The risk is limited to validators, schema generators, or XML pipelines that previously depended on `ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath` rather than evaluating FHIRPath. Such tooling may silently skip the local Count rule or miss the added non-negative check unless it is updated.

justification.inferredGoal: Prefer FHIRPath as the computable constraint language in the R6 StructureDefinition package.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain an auxiliary XPath translation for `Count.cnt-3` while making the R6 FHIRPath expression authoritative.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This finding is not an instance-validity break, but it can break metadata consumers that depended on `ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath`. The inferred goal of relying on a single authoritative FHIRPath constraint language is reasonable, especially because R6 still supplies the computable FHIRPath expression. Retaining XPath would have been less disruptive for legacy XML validators, but it would perpetuate dual-expression maintenance and stale translations; the R4 XPath already would not express the stricter R6 non-negative rule without revision.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept an XPath form for the local `cnt-3` invariant as non-authoritative or generated metadata. That would preserve most legacy XPath-based validator and code-generation workflows while still allowing FHIRPath-first validation. The alternative is partial because it likely depends on broader R6 `ElementDefinition` support for XPath and requires maintaining equivalence between two constraint languages; across the specification, some FHIRPath rules may be difficult or unsafe to translate exactly.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Eases XPath-only tooling but requires maintaining a second expression, including the new non-negative clause, with divergence risk and broader implementation burden.

evidence.detail: R4 supplies an XPath expression for the local `cnt-3` invariant.
evidence.quote: (f:code or not(f:value)) and (not(exists(f:system)) or (f:system/@value='http://unitsofmeasure.org' and f:code/@value='1')) and not(contains(f:value/@value, '.'))

evidence.detail: R6 supplies `expression` and `source` for `cnt-3`, with no `xpath` property in the local constraint object.

examples.examplesMd: There is no instance fragment for this finding because the change is in StructureDefinition metadata consumed by validators and generators, not in the JSON/XML shape of `Count` instances.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a tooling migration risk rather than an instance compatibility break. Implementations that still translate or execute R4 XPath constraints for XML validation cannot assume an R6 XPath expression is available for `Count.cnt-3`. They need FHIRPath support to enforce the local Count rule, including the new non-negative requirement.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Instance compatibility is unaffected by the missing XPath property itself. Runtime compatibility is affected only for metadata consumers that require XPath constraints. A FHIRPath-capable R6 validator can still enforce the invariant; an XPath-only validator may under-validate R6 `Count` values.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update validation and code-generation pipelines to treat FHIRPath as the authoritative constraint source. If XML-only validation is required, derive and test a local XPath equivalent for `cnt-3`, including the added non-negative clause, rather than reusing the R4 XPath expression.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The backward-compatible alternative would be to keep the XPath field for this invariant. That would ease legacy XML validator migration but would also risk divergence because the R4 XPath did not include the new non-negative test.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This likely reflects a broader R6 StructureDefinition representation change. It is included here only because the omitted XPath belonged to Count's own local `cnt-3` invariant.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The R4 `cnt-3` constraint carried an XPath expression, while the R6 constraint carries the FHIRPath expression and source but no XPath metadata. This does not make any Count instance valid or invalid on its own and does not alter the wire path, cardinality, type, or binding. The plausible affected scenario is an old XML/XPath-based validator or generator that depends on `ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath`; that tool must rely on FHIRPath or update its R6 support. That is tooling metadata churn rather than a path-level compatibility break in exchanged Count data.
keyEvidence: R6 `StructureDefinition-Count.json` `differential.element[id=Count].constraint[key=cnt-3]` includes `expression` and `source` and has no `xpath` property.
The structural Count elements and the `cnt-3` FHIRPath constraint remain present in R6; only the XPath metadata is absent for this finding.
freshReview.fmmEffect: The R4 baseline is trial-use, which further softens concern for metadata/tooling churn. Even under higher maturity this would not be an instance-level break because it is not a data model change.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling: legacy tooling that consumed XPath metadata may need updates, but exchanged instances are unaffected by the metadata field's absence.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained a non-normative XPath companion for legacy XML validators, but doing so would preserve obsolete duplicate constraint metadata and risk divergence from FHIRPath. Because the compatibility issue is only tooling metadata, a less-breaking base design is not necessary.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing low-impact/runtime-tooling assessment, but the fresh judgment treats this as metadata/tooling churn with no meaningful compatibility problem rather than a substantive break.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: `Count` exists in both packages with the same canonical URL, id, name, type, kind, abstract flag, derivation, and `Quantity` base definition. Metadata status changed, but identity did not.

The snapshot element ids remain `Count`, `Count.id`, `Count.extension`, `Count.value`, `Count.comparator`, `Count.unit`, `Count.system`, and `Count.code`. No local element was added, removed, renamed, moved, split, or merged.
All compared `Count` snapshot element cardinalities are unchanged: root `0..*`, `id` `0..1`, `extension` `0..*`, and `value`, `comparator`, `unit`, `system`, and `code` each `0..1`.

The local element type codes are unchanged: `value` remains `decimal`, `comparator` and `code` remain `code`, `unit` remains `string`, `system` remains `uri`, `extension` remains `Extension`, and `id` remains FHIRPath `System.String`.
`Count` has no Reference-typed local elements, so no reference target changes apply.

No binding is introduced by the local `Count` differential. The required `Quantity.comparator` binding changes from the R4 to R6 value set version and the R6 code system adds `ad`, but this is inherited from `Quantity` and excluded from local findings.
No fixed value, pattern, or default value constraints were found on the local `Count` differential in either version.
`Count.comparator` remains the only modifier element in the snapshot, and `Count` itself remains `isModifier: false`.
Summary flags are unchanged for the `Count` snapshot: `value`, `comparator`, `unit`, `system`, and `code` are summary elements; `id` and `extension` are not.
`Count.extension` remains open-sliced by `url`; no local Count slicing rule changed.

The root short, definition, and comment are materially unchanged. R6 package-level description removes the R4 phrase `Base StructureDefinition for`, which is editorial. The `cnt-3` human text did not change even though the expression became stricter.

The local R6 non-negative rule narrows the R4 value domain, so it does not create a local R6-to-R4 representability problem. The inherited `Quantity.comparator` `ad` code is a separate R6-to-R4 risk owned by the `Quantity` analysis.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Count metadata moved from draft/trial-use to active/normative
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is standards-status and lifecycle metadata. It does not change the JSON/XML element shape, cardinalities, local types, or instance validation by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance processes may treat the R6 datatype as more stable or harder to vary, but implementations do not need an instance transform for this metadata change.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds `has-range` type-characteristic metadata to Count
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The new `structuredefinition-type-characteristics` extension is metadata on the StructureDefinition. It does not add a required instance element or reject an R4 instance.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators or modeling tools that consume R6 type characteristics may expose `Count` differently, but this should be additive metadata handling rather than an instance migration requirement.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 description removes the R4 `Base StructureDefinition for` prefix
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The substantive Count definition remains the same. The description wording change is editorial and does not alter validation or data meaning.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Documentation comparisons should not treat this prefix removal as a datatype identity change.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `Count` inherits `value`, `comparator`, `unit`, `system`, and `code` from `Quantity`. R6 inherited changes include comparator terminology expansion with code `ad`, the `qty-4` UCUM annotation warning, and `Quantity` base-definition/type-characteristic shifts. Those should be assessed in the `Quantity` report.
`Count.id` and `Count.extension` behavior, inherited `ele-1`/`ext-1` constraint representation, and the broader R6 datatype base hierarchy are base-artifact concerns excluded from this local report.

The R6 comparator CodeSystem adds `ad`. This affects `Count.comparator` only through inherited `Quantity.comparator`; it should be reconciled with the `Quantity` terminology finding rather than duplicated here.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official Count-specific R4-to-R6 diff or ballot change note was available in the local inputs. The report therefore identifies computable deltas but infers intent and justification from the StructureDefinition content.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A published HL7 change note, Jira ticket, or official diff explaining the `cnt-3` non-negative addition would improve confidence in the rationale and migration expectations.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Full rendered datatype narrative pages were not consulted. The R6 StructureDefinition contains generated narrative, but not all surrounding explanatory text or ballot context.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Reviewing the official rendered R4 and R6 datatype pages could confirm whether prose outside the StructureDefinition explains non-negative Count semantics.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology server expansion was not run. The inherited Quantity comparator difference was checked only by comparing local CodeSystem files and was not promoted to a local Count finding.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A terminology expansion and official cross-version terminology map would improve confidence for inherited `Quantity.comparator` migration, handled outside this report.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The new input is an R6 ballot build package, not a final published release. Later ballots or publication may change the `Count` invariant, metadata, or rendered narrative.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run this assessment against the final R6 core package when available.
